title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1LC0RE_1LE0LD_0LB1LB_1RA0LF_1LD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RA_1LC0RE_1LE0LD_0LB1LB_1RA0LF_1LD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. With u = 1110, at the right extensions the tape is a few large blocks u^x separated by short defects (1^k, 1^2 0, u^2). The leftward sweeps turn each block into a block of w = 10011110 (the sweeps over 8-cell words are proved in Lean) and the rightward sweeps turn it back. The large blocks grow and split irregularly (104, 108, 96, 41 at step 1.8·106; 3608, 11238, 1167, 526, 783 at step 4.8·109); the width grows like √t. The block rule is not known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 31,819 cells have been visited and 22,003 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.515). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.282).

claims.title: Sweep rules
claims.text:
The head sweeps over long runs of a repeated word, rewriting each copy, for any number n of copies and any surrounding tape. Examples:
  • L A> (1)^n R → L (1)^n A> R
  • L A> (01001111)^n R → L (01110111)^n A> R
  • L A> (10100111)^n R → L (10111011)^n A> R
  • L (10100111)^n B> 0 R → L B> 0 (01001111)^n R
Generated by py/rules.py (tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py).

claims.title: Few large blocks
claims.text: At the 960 extensions up to 6·109 steps (tools/c/tokrun, w = 10011110, u = 1110), the blocks longer than 20 copies of u at the right extensions are 888, 1502, 22, 120, 286 (step 1.25·108), 2000, 5064, 646, 983 (step 1.36·109) and 3608, 11238, 1167, 526, 783 (step 4.80·109).

claims.title: Square-root width
claims.text: The width is 19,664 at step 3.95·10<sup>8</sup> and 69,788 at step 4.80·10<sup>9</sup>, about √t.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The decider pipeline of bbchallenge left it open; no proof either way is recorded here yet.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 31,819 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Blocks and defects
html:
Write u for 1110 and w for 10011110. At step 4,797,529,835 (head in E at the right end) the tape is

u^3608 1^5 u^2 1^3 u^11238 1^3 u^2 1^2 u^2 1^2 0 u^1167 1^7 u^2 1^374 u^4 1^6 u^526 1^8 u^2 1 u^2 1^3 u^783 1^2 0 u^3 1^2 0^2 E>

and at the next left extension (step 4,797,881,171) the same blocks read as w^1804 ... w^5618 ... w^583 ...: the leftward sweep rewrites each pair of us as one w.

sections.heading: How the blocks change
html: The defects between blocks (runs of 1s of length 1 to a few hundred) change on every sweep and the blocks grow, shrink and split irregularly. No rule is known; a halt (F reading 1) has not occurred in 6·109 steps.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.515). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.282).
After 109 steps the tape spans 31,819 cells (21,492 left of the start, 1,068 right), with a density of 1s of 0.692.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A list of a few large blocks of 1110 separated by short defects (runs of 1s, 0s), which the sweeps rewrite into blocks of 10011110 and back. Block sizes change irregularly (3608, 11238, 1167, 526, 783 at step 4.8*10^9) and the width grows like the square root of the step count. Counter-like, not understood; halting open.
